# Two branches each add a different user. The audit-log merge driver rebases
# theirs' user.tell onto ours, so the merged log holds both users, records a
# merge entry, and chain-verifies.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# OURS: add bob.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add bob'

# THEIRS: branch off the init commit and add carol.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: add carol'

# Merge THEIRS into OURS. The audit-log driver merges the log but always reports
# a conflict (exit 1) so git stops before committing - the user must seal and
# commit, which runs the pre-commit verify. (sesam.yml also conflicts; that is a
# known, accepted gap for now.)
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs

# The merged audit log is in the worktree: it chain-verifies, and holds both
# user.tell entries plus a merge entry. (State is asserted via the log, not
# `sesam user list`, because that reads the still-conflicted sesam.yml.)
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk

exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"user": "bob"'
stdout '"user": "carol"'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'
